Let’s talk about something that’s on just about everyone’s mind at some point—success.
Or maybe, how we’re supposed to define it.
This chapter is called Redefining Success and Self-Worth, and honestly, isn’t that what your twenties are all about?
Think about all the pressure that comes with being young today. There’s this checklist—land the right job, find the perfect partner, buy that house, tick every box.
But what if your story doesn’t match that script?
Here’s where our main character finds herself, sitting in a sunny park while She-Devil, her loyal companion, stretches out by her feet. She’s watching people go by—families, couples, folks wandering alone—and it suddenly hits her: everyone out there is carrying their own version of success and failure, and most of it’s invisible to anyone else.
It’s a moment that’s both humbling and, honestly, a little freeing.
She starts to notice the little things that bring her real joy. Maybe it’s a book she can’t put down, a walk in the rain, or a conversation that leaves her feeling heard and understood. These aren’t exactly Instagram-worthy, but they’re the moments that make her life feel meaningful.
And suddenly, that pressure to keep up, to perform, starts to feel a little less heavy.
When she talks with friends, she realizes she’s not alone in this. There’s a sense of relief in letting go of someone else’s idea of success. Most of us don’t even notice how much happier we are until we stop chasing those old definitions.
Redefining self-worth isn’t a one-and-done thing, of course. There are setbacks and breakthroughs, and some days are definitely easier than others. But with every step, the need for outside approval fades and real self-acceptance starts to grow.
And through it all, there’s She-Devil—completely unaware of human ambitions, loving her person just the same. Her joy is simple, her needs are few, and she never judges.
Being with her, it’s easier to believe that you don’t have to prove anything to be worthy.
After all, maybe being enough isn’t about what you achieve—it’s about who you are, right here, right now.
